title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery — Offset-History Rates on Withholding Proposals
content:
The withholding a debtor has already suffered on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** sets an offset rate on the monthly withholding proposed on a reduced-withholding request.

**Rule.** When four or more benefit offsets posted on the debt in the last six calendar months counted back from today, the long-offset rate of 90 percent applies. When one to three did, the short-offset rate of 95 percent applies. When none did, no offset rate applies.

A benefit offset is an amount withheld from a VA benefit payment and applied to the debt; direct payments do not count. A record falls in the last six calendar months when fewer than six whole calendar months have passed from its date to today: on 20 October, 21 April counts and 20 April does not. The offset rate is a percentage by which the starting figure of the proposal is multiplied before the proposal is rounded up to the cent.

| Benefit offsets posted on the debt in the period | Offset rate |
|---|---|
| 4 or more | 90 percent |
| 1, 2 or 3 | 95 percent |
| None | None |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical).** Three offsets in the period: 95 percent. A fourth offset posting: 90 percent. Offsets only older than six months: none.
